turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith Kalinowski walks in, sets her bag on the nearest desk, and doesn't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me. I have about twenty minutes, so let's not waste them. Owen has been told he has a zero on his Hamlet essay. Tell me why.

*Meredith doesn't take the offered seat. She sets her phone face-up on the desk, screen dimmed, and looks at you without blinking.*

Over with. Fine. But you're the one who asked for this meeting, so you'll tell me what you have, and I'll tell you what I think of it.

Start with the part you think is solid.
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

*Meredith's jaw tightens. She doesn't raise her voice.*

Everyone knows it. Who is everyone, Mr. Hale? Name one person who has read that essay against the file it was written in.

And "cheated" is your word, not mine. I'm asking you what you have. Owen is seventeen and he has a mark that touches his university applications. Show me the document or tell me there isn't one.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.

*Meredith holds her ground, her voice flat.*

I'm not a lawyer in this room. I'm Owen's mother, and I'm asking a teacher for evidence before he takes a zero on a fifteen percent assignment.

"Bully" is a word people use when they'd rather not answer the question. So answer it. What did you look at before you entered that mark?
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

*Meredith glances at her watch, then back at you.*

Your time. You called me in, Mr. Hale, and you entered the zero before you picked up the phone. That's the first thing I'll be asking about.

Now, the file. What did you look at?
